details: The 30-year U.S. Treasury yield climbed to 5.2% on May 19, 2026, reaching its highest level since 2007. This surge is primarily driven by deepening inflation fears, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict in Iran, and concerns over unsustainable government finances. Rising yields increase borrowing costs across the U.S. economy and make safer investments more attractive, consequently dampening investor appetite for riskier assets like cryptocurrencies.
title: US 30-Year Treasury Yields Soar to 2007 Highs, Pressuring Risk Assets

details: In a significant geopolitical development, Iran is reportedly leveraging Bitcoin to offer shipping insurance for vessels transiting the Strait of Hormuz. This initiative, named "Hormuz Safe," aims to generate substantial revenue (potentially up to $10 billion) and reduce Iran's reliance on the dollar system, thereby circumventing international sanctions. The ongoing U.S.-Iran standoff and the resulting disruption in the critical waterway are contributing to elevated oil prices and global economic uncertainty, which broadly impacts financial markets and heightens risk aversion.
title: Iran Reportedly Uses Bitcoin for Strait of Hormuz Shipping Insurance Amid Tensions

details: The U.S. Consumer Price Index (CPI) for April 2026 rose 3.8% year-over-year, marking the fastest pace since May 2023. This hotter-than-expected inflation data, primarily driven by escalating energy costs and persistent core price pressures, has significantly shifted market expectations regarding Federal Reserve policy. Traders are now pricing in a near-zero chance of rate cuts through the end of 2027, with some even considering the possibility of future rate hikes to combat entrenched inflation.
title: US CPI Inflation Surges to 3.8%, Dampening Rate Cut Hopes

details: Kevin Warsh has been confirmed as the new Chair of the U.S. Federal Reserve. While President Trump had advocated for aggressive interest rate cuts, Warsh now faces a challenging economic landscape. Recent inflation data showing a 3.8% year-over-year CPI increase for April, coupled with rising Producer Price Index (PPI) figures, suggests that the new Fed Chair may be compelled to consider maintaining higher rates or even implementing hikes rather than easing monetary policy. This stance could limit liquidity and negatively impact risk-on assets, including cryptocurrencies.
title: Kevin Warsh Confirmed as New Fed Chair Amidst Inflationary Headwinds

details: Crypto investment products recorded substantial net outflows of $1.07 billion last week, marking the third-largest weekly outflow of the year. Bitcoin funds were hit particularly hard, with $982 million in redemptions, ending a six-week streak of inflows. This trend indicates a notable shift in institutional sentiment, reflecting increasing caution among investors in response to deteriorating global macroeconomic conditions and heightened market uncertainty.
title: Crypto Funds Experience Significant Outflows Amid Macroeconomic Pressures

details: Poland's parliament has successfully approved a bill to integrate the European Union's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation into its national legal framework. This crucial step aims to bring regulatory clarity and enhance oversight within the Polish crypto market, ensuring compliance with the EU's July deadline. The move is expected to strengthen investor protection and foster a more stable environment for digital asset businesses, despite occurring amidst an ongoing investigation into a local crypto exchange that has highlighted the need for stricter regulations.
title: Poland Passes Landmark MiCA Crypto Regulation Law
